newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Ramos wants to stay longer in office but is "too shy" to ask for the lifting of the constitutional limit on his term, Budget Secretary Salvador Enriquez said yesterday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- At least seven senior police officials who are closely associated with President Ramos have been promoted in the latest round of revamp in the National Police. (TIMES)
- A big kidnap gang in Metro Manila has shifted its operations to Mindanao where 67 people have been abducted this year, according to sources in the intelligence community. (INQUIRER)
- Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, the country's second largest oil company, lowered the prices of its liquefied petroleum gas and diesel. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Philippine Central Bank stepped in yesterday at the foreign exchange market to halt the speculative attack against the peso by selling dollars and hiking the overnight borrowing rate to 15 percent. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Land Bank of the Philippines yesterday foreclosed properties of Victorias Milling Corp unit North Negros Marketing Corp for failure to pay 465 million pesos. (TODAY/INQUIRER)
